```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 7)
```

Many infections have a **latent period**: a person is infected but not yet
infectious. The SEIR model adds an **E**xposed compartment:

$$
\frac{dS}{dt} = -\beta \frac{SI}{N}, \quad
\frac{dE}{dt} = \beta \frac{SI}{N} - \sigma E, \quad
\frac{dI}{dt} = \sigma E - \gamma I, \quad
\frac{dR}{dt} = \gamma I
$$

where $\sigma = 1/(\text{latent period})$. Here we use a 5-day latent period
($\sigma = 0.2$).

```{r}
library(deSolve)

seir <- function(time, state, parms) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parms)), {
    dS <- -beta * S * I / N
    dE <-  beta * S * I / N - sigma * E
    dI <-  sigma * E - gamma * I
    dR <-  gamma * I
    list(c(dS, dE, dI, dR))
  })
}

sir <- function(time, state, parms) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parms)), {
    dS <- -beta * S * I / N
    dI <-  beta * S * I / N - gamma * I
    dR <-  gamma * I
    list(c(dS, dI, dR))
  })
}

N <- 1000
times <- seq(0, 200, by = 1)

seir_out <- as.data.frame(ode(c(S = N - 1, E = 0, I = 1, R = 0), times, seir,
                              c(beta = 0.5, sigma = 0.2, gamma = 0.2, N = N)))
sir_out  <- as.data.frame(ode(c(S = N - 1, I = 1, R = 0), times, sir,
                              c(beta = 0.5, gamma = 0.2, N = N)))
```

# SIR vs SEIR

```{r}
plot(sir_out$time, sir_out$I, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "red",
     xlab = "Day", ylab = "Infectious people", ylim = c(0, 350))
lines(seir_out$time, seir_out$I, lwd = 2, col = "blue")
legend("topright", c("SIR", "SEIR"), col = c("red", "blue"), lwd = 2)
```

```{r}
data.frame(
  model = c("SIR", "SEIR"),
  peak_day = c(sir_out$time[which.max(sir_out$I)], seir_out$time[which.max(seir_out$I)]),
  peak_infectious = round(c(max(sir_out$I), max(seir_out$I)))
)
```

Both models have the same $R_0 = \beta/\gamma = 2.5$, so they share the same
final size, but the latent period **delays** the epidemic and lowers the peak
of the infectious curve.
